files.what_it_shows: The whole 5.8 mile, 16 inch McCloud Lateral on an Open Street Map basemap at 1 to 20,000. It starts at the existing El Paso Compressor Station in the lower left, runs north in a stepped path across vacant land past Stan Roberts Sr Avenue, then runs east along the New Mexico and Texas state line to the McCloud Meter Station at the upper right. The magenta line is the pipeline centerline and the black outline is the limit of disturbance.
landmarks: New Mexico and Texas state line

searched: FERC eLibrary docket CP26-558 file list through the search service (found the prior notice filing of July 30, 2026, the environmental assessment report, protests and data request responses)
The Federal Register notice of August 10, 2026, which gave the docket number
The public volume 1 of the application and its Resource Report 1 attachment, read for figures
The oilandgaswatch record has no attached documents, so none were available there
notes: The map is clear and shows the full length of the lateral. The route is entirely in El Paso County, Texas, except for a 120 foot permanent access road in Otero County, New Mexico, which the report names in a footnote. The sheet's start and end state of Texas is right. Resource Report 1 also has Appendix 1A, topographic maps on a USGS basemap (figure 1A-1, many sheets), which would help if a finer fit is wanted. The alignment sheets themselves were filed as CEII (Critical Energy Infrastructure Information) and are not public. The FERC download page is a JavaScript application, so the URL checker calls it a JavaScript shell and cannot read it; the file itself was downloaded and read with pdftotext and pdftoppm. The report was prepared by Tetra Tech for El Paso Natural Gas Company, L.L.C. and the drawing is marked as a privileged draft in the footer even though FERC filed it as public.
